source.paper_title: RUNLTS: Register-value-aware Predictor Utilizing Nested Large Tables
source.citation: Toru Koizumi, Toshiki Maekawa, Masanari Mizuno, Maru Kuroki, Tomoaki Tsumura, and Ryota Shioya. 2025. RUNLTS: Register-value-aware Predictor Utilizing Nested Large Tables. In Proceedings of the 6th Championship Branch Prediction (CBP 2025), June 21, 2025, Tokyo, Japan.

summary: The sR component is a register-value-aware statistical corrector (SC) extension that improves branch prediction accuracy by exploiting correlations between recently produced architectural register values and conditional branch outcomes. Rather than tracking register dependencies or computing arithmetic differences between branch operands, sR globally monitors all logical registers using a 12-bit digest representation tailored to data types (integer leading/trailing zero/one patterns and LSBs, floating-point sign and exponent slices, or replicated condition flags). A Tomasulo-like tracking table records register availability and invalidates entries after 256 decoded instructions to discard stale values. During branch prediction, available registers within each of eight banks are evaluated for prediction usefulness using per-register usefulness tables; the digest of the most useful available register in each bank is hashed with the branch PC to index three prediction weight tables. Each bank's prediction contribution is scaled by 2.5 if deemed useful (or suppressed to 0 if not), and the contributions across all banks are summed into the SC's LSUM to bias or override the base TAGE prediction.

state.name: register_tracking_table
state.organization: Direct-mapped, 65 entries (1 entry per logical register: R0..R64)
state.entry_format: valid: 1 bit, payload: 14 bits (holds 14-bit in-flight ROB tag when valid=0, or 12-bit value digest when valid=1), decay_ctr: 8 bits (saturating instruction counter)
state.indexing: Directly indexed by logical register index (0 to 64; 8 or 9 registers per bank across 8 banks)

state.name: usefulness_weight_tables
state.organization: 8 banks; each bank contains 3 usefulness tables (UT0, UT1, UT2) of 8 entries each. Bank 0 covers 9 logical registers (r % 8 == 0); Banks 1..7 cover 8 logical registers each
state.entry_format: Bank 0: 9 x 6-bit signed saturating weights (54 bits per entry); Banks 1..7: 8 x 6-bit signed saturating weights (48 bits per entry). Counter range: [-32, 31]
state.indexing: 3-bit index derived from branch PC hashed/skewed independently per table (PC_skewed into UT0, UT1, UT2)

state.name: prediction_weight_tables
state.organization: 8 banks; each bank contains 3 weight tables: WT0 (512 entries), WT1 (256 entries), WT2 (128 entries)
state.entry_format: 1 x 6-bit signed saturating weight per entry. Counter range: [-32, 31]
state.indexing: Hash of branch PC and selected register 12-bit digest: WT0 indexed by 9-bit hash h0(PC, digest), WT1 indexed by 8-bit hash h1(PC, digest), WT2 indexed by 7-bit hash h2(PC, digest)

algorithms.name: digest_generation
algorithms.trigger: Instruction execution completion / writeback when a new register value is produced
algorithms.notes: Produces a 12-bit digest from a 64-bit value. For integer registers, overlapping fields are XOR-folded. For floating-point registers, bits [2:0] are unused (0). For condition-code flags, the 4 flag bits are replicated across nibbles.

algorithms.name: register_decode_dispatch
algorithms.trigger: Instruction decode / rename stage in host pipeline
algorithms.notes: Clears valid bit when an instruction renaming destination register rd enters the pipeline and records the ROB tag. All valid digests age by 1 on every decoded instruction; entries reach staleness and are invalidated when decay_ctr reaches 256.

algorithms.name: register_writeback
algorithms.notes: When an in-flight instruction completes execution, matching ROB tag updates the payload with the 12-bit value digest, sets valid=1, and resets the decay counter.

algorithms.name: pipeline_squash
algorithms.trigger: Branch misprediction recovery / backend pipeline squash
algorithms.notes: Entries that completed execution prior to or during the flush remain valid=1 with their digests preserved; this expands the visible register values available immediately after the flush, enabling RUNLTS to correct subsequent mispredictions.

algorithms.name: predict
algorithms.trigger: Branch prediction lookup time at fetch/frontend
algorithms.pseudocode:
function predict_sr(pc):
    sR_sum = 0
    for bank in 0 .. 7:
        regs_in_bank = get_logical_regs_for_bank(bank) // 9 regs for bank 0, 8 regs for banks 1..7
        valid_regs = [r for r in regs_in_bank if register_tracking_table[r].valid == 1]

        if length(valid_regs) == 0:
            bank_contrib[bank] = 0
            chosen_reg[bank] = NULL
            continue

        // Compute usefulness per valid register from 3 UT tables
        idx0 = hash_ut0(pc, bank)
        idx1 = hash_ut1(pc, bank)
        idx2 = hash_ut2(pc, bank)

        best_reg = valid_regs[0]
        max_useful = -9999
        for r in valid_regs:
            offset = get_reg_bank_offset(bank, r)
            u_val = usefulness_weight_tables[bank].UT0[idx0][offset] +
                    usefulness_weight_tables[bank].UT1[idx1][offset] +
                    usefulness_weight_tables[bank].UT2[idx2][offset]
            if u_val > max_useful:
                max_useful = u_val
                best_reg = r

        chosen_reg[bank] = best_reg
        chosen_useful[bank] = max_useful

        // Query prediction weight tables using chosen register digest
        digest = register_tracking_table[best_reg].payload & 0x0FFF
        h0 = hash_wt0(pc, digest) // 9 bits -> 512 entries
        h1 = hash_wt1(pc, digest) // 8 bits -> 256 entries
        h2 = hash_wt2(pc, digest) // 7 bits -> 128 entries

        sum_wt = prediction_weight_tables[bank].WT0[h0] +
                 prediction_weight_tables[bank].WT1[h1] +
                 prediction_weight_tables[bank].WT2[h2]

        // Useful scaling stage: x0 or x2.5
        if max_useful > 0:
            bank_contrib[bank] = sum_wt * 2.5
        else:
            bank_contrib[bank] = 0

        sR_sum += bank_contrib[bank]

    return sR_sum
algorithms.notes: Bank membership: logical register r belongs to bank (r % 8). Bank 0 contains 9 registers (R0, R8, ..., R64); banks 1..7 contain 8 registers each. Multiplier is applied per bank: x2.5 if bank usefulness is positive, x0 if negative/zero or if no register in the bank was valid. Scaled bank contributions are summed to produce sR, which feeds into SC LSUM.

algorithms.name: update
algorithms.trigger: Branch update / retirement time (when SC update condition is met: misprediction or |LSUM| <= update_threshold)
algorithms.pseudocode:
function update_sr(pc, actual_dir, checkpointed_state):
    for bank in 0 .. 7:
        avail_regs = checkpointed_state.available_regs_at_pred[bank]
        if length(avail_regs) == 0:
            continue

        // Randomly select one available register within this bank for single-port update
        selected_reg = pseudo_random_choice(avail_regs)
        offset = get_reg_bank_offset(bank, selected_reg)
        digest = checkpointed_state.reg_digest[selected_reg]

        // 1. Update usefulness weights for selected register
        // Incremented if the prediction was useful / aligned with outcome, decremented otherwise
        was_useful = (checkpointed_state.bank_wt_sum[bank] >= 0) == (actual_dir == TAKEN)
        delta_u = +1 if was_useful else -1

        idx0 = hash_ut0(pc, bank)
        idx1 = hash_ut1(pc, bank)
        idx2 = hash_ut2(pc, bank)
        usefulness_weight_tables[bank].UT0[idx0][offset] = saturating_add(usefulness_weight_tables[bank].UT0[idx0][offset], delta_u, -32, 31)
        usefulness_weight_tables[bank].UT1[idx1][offset] = saturating_add(usefulness_weight_tables[bank].UT1[idx1][offset], delta_u, -32, 31)
        usefulness_weight_tables[bank].UT2[idx2][offset] = saturating_add(usefulness_weight_tables[bank].UT2[idx2][offset], delta_u, -32, 31)

        // 2. Update prediction weights for selected register digest
        delta_w = +1 if actual_dir == TAKEN else -1
        h0 = hash_wt0(pc, digest)
        h1 = hash_wt1(pc, digest)
        h2 = hash_wt2(pc, digest)
        prediction_weight_tables[bank].WT0[h0] = saturating_add(prediction_weight_tables[bank].WT0[h0], delta_w, -32, 31)
        prediction_weight_tables[bank].WT1[h1] = saturating_add(prediction_weight_tables[bank].WT1[h1], delta_w, -32, 31)
        prediction_weight_tables[bank].WT2[h2] = saturating_add(prediction_weight_tables[bank].WT2[h2], delta_w, -32, 31)
algorithms.notes: Single write port requirement: during training, updates occur only for registers available at prediction time. If multiple registers were available in a bank, exactly one is randomly chosen. Weights saturate as 6-bit signed integers in range [-32, 31].

host_interfaces.need: instruction decode / destination register rename signals
host_interfaces.description: Host notifies predictor at decode/rename with destination logical register index and assigned ROB tag to clear valid bit and track pending status
host_interfaces.fallback: If ROB tags are unavailable at rename, use an in-order architectural register tracker where values update only at architectural retirement; however, this disables misprediction recovery latency advantages.

host_interfaces.need: execution complete / register writeback signals and values
host_interfaces.description: Host forwards produced 64-bit register value, register type (INT, FP, FLAGS), destination register ID, and matching ROB tag upon execution completion
host_interfaces.fallback: Generate 12-bit digests at commit/retirement instead of execution completion. Digests will only reflect committed state rather than speculative post-flush in-flight values.

host_interfaces.need: instruction decode / commit stream count for staleness aging
host_interfaces.description: Host provides a per-cycle or per-instruction decode count to advance the 8-bit decay counters in the register tracking table
host_interfaces.fallback: Use branch instruction count or cycle count sampled periodically (e.g. advance decay every 16 cycles or every 32 branches).

host_interfaces.need: pipeline squash / flush notifications with ROB scope
host_interfaces.description: Host signals branch misprediction squash along with the range of squashed ROB tags to clear uncommitted in-flight destination register reservations
host_interfaces.fallback: Reset all invalid entries in the register tracking table to clean state upon squash, retaining only entries that were marked valid with completed digests.

host_interfaces.need: statistical corrector LSUM integration and update trigger
host_interfaces.description: Host SC summation tree must incorporate sR as one of the additive partial sums contributing to LSUM, and host must supply SC update trigger and branch outcome at commit
host_interfaces.fallback: If used standalone without full SC, sR can be thresholded against zero to provide a standalone direction prediction or override bimodal prediction.

resource_accounting.storage_breakdown: Prediction weight tables (WT): 8 banks x (512 + 256 + 128) entries x 6 bits = 43,008 bits. Usefulness weight tables (UT): 6 bits x 65 registers x (8 + 8 + 8) entries = 9,360 bits (Bank 0: 3 tables x 8 entries x 9 regs x 6 bits = 1,296 bits; Banks 1..7: 7 banks x 3 tables x 8 entries x 8 regs x 6 bits = 8,064 bits). Auxiliary tracking table: 65 entries x (1 bit valid + 14 bits payload + 8 bits decay_ctr) = 1,495 bits. Total = 43,008 + 9,360 + 1,495 = 53,863 bits (6.57 KiB).
resource_accounting.logic_cost_notes: Requires 12-bit digest generation units (leading/trailing zero/one counters and XOR trees for INT, bit-slicers for FP/FLAGS), an 8-way parallel usefulness argmax tree per bank (comparing 8 or 9 6-bit values), three-input adders per bank, fixed-point x2.5 multiplier (shift-and-add: x2 + x0.5), an 8-input adder tree for cross-bank sR summation, and a pseudo-random generator/LFSR for update bank register arbitration.
resource_accounting.budget_donors: To fit within an iso-storage budget (e.g., 64 KiB or 192 KiB), storage can be reclaimed by reducing entry counts in SC local history tables (sC, sL, sS, sT) or by reducing the number of high-bank tagged entries in TAGE.

parameters.name: num_banks
parameters.storage_impact: Scales the number of WT banks linearly; affects bank distribution of logical registers and UT width.

parameters.name: num_logical_registers
parameters.storage_impact: Directly scales the register tracking table (23 bits per register) and the total number of usefulness weights in UT (144 bits per register).

parameters.name: wt0_entries
parameters.storage_impact: Adds num_banks * wt0_entries * 6 bits to total storage.

parameters.name: wt1_entries
parameters.storage_impact: Adds num_banks * wt1_entries * 6 bits to total storage.

parameters.name: wt2_entries
parameters.storage_impact: Adds num_banks * wt2_entries * 6 bits to total storage.

parameters.name: weight_bits
parameters.storage_impact: Scales WT and UT storage linearly with weight bit-width.

parameters.name: decay_interval
parameters.storage_impact: Log2(decay_interval) determines the width of decay_ctr (8 bits for 256), impacting auxiliary tracking table size.

parameters.name: useful_multiplier
parameters.storage_impact: No storage impact; adjusts fixed scaling factor logic in prediction datapath.

unit_tests.name: int_digest_generation_folding
unit_tests.given: An integer register R0 produced with value 0x0000000000000005 (binary 0...0101: trailing zeros = 0, leading zeros = 61, LSBs = 5)

unit_tests.name: fp64_digest_generation_sign_exponent
unit_tests.given: An FP64 register containing IEEE-754 double precision value 1.0 (0x3FF0000000000000): sign = 0, exp = 0x3FF (1023)
unit_tests.expect: Value[63:55] is extracted: sign bit 63 (0) followed by 8 MSBs of exponent bits [62:55] (01111111_2 = 0x7F), placed at digest bits [11:3]. Expected digest = (0x07F << 3) = 0x03F8, with digest bits [2:0] = 0.

unit_tests.name: flags_digest_replication
unit_tests.given: A condition-code register producing 4-bit flag value 0b1011 (0x0B)
unit_tests.expect: The 4 bits are replicated 3 times into a 12-bit digest: (0xB << 8) | (0xB << 4) | 0xB = 0xBBB.

unit_tests.name: register_tracking_table_aging_and_decay
unit_tests.given: A valid digest loaded into entry R8 at cycle 0 with decay_ctr = 0, followed by 256 subsequent instruction decodes without new writes to R8
unit_tests.expect: decay_ctr increments on each decode up to 255. On the 256th decode, the entry is invalidated (valid bit cleared to 0) and ceases to be considered in branch prediction.

unit_tests.name: bank_usefulness_selection_and_multiplier
unit_tests.given: Bank 0 has valid registers R0 and R8. PC indexes UT tables such that R0 usefulness sum is -2 and R8 usefulness sum is +5. WT tables for R8 evaluate to sum_wt = +4
unit_tests.expect: R8 is chosen as the most useful register in Bank 0 because +5 > -2. Since usefulness (+5) > 0, the x2.5 multiplier activates, producing a bank contribution of 4 * 2.5 = +10.0 towards sR.

unit_tests.name: bank_suppression_on_non_positive_usefulness
unit_tests.given: Bank 1 has valid register R1 with usefulness sum -3 and WT sum +8
unit_tests.expect: Because maximum usefulness is <= 0, the x0 multiplier activates, suppressing Bank 1 contribution to 0.0 despite the positive WT weight.

unit_tests.name: single_write_port_random_arbitration_on_update
unit_tests.given: At prediction time, Bank 2 had three available valid registers {R2, R10, R18}. The branch mispredicts and triggers SC update
unit_tests.expect: The update logic pseudo-randomly selects exactly one of {R2, R10, R18} to update its corresponding UT and WT entries, requiring strictly 1 write port per table.

open_questions: Leading/trailing count semantics in Section 4.2 / Figure 6(a): whether the count saturates at 63, counts bits matching the sign bit, or counts strictly zeros versus ones based on an MSB/LSB flag bit (as 0..64 requires 7 bits but the field is 6 bits wide). Default assumed: saturates at 63.

Floating-point format classification: the exact criteria used to inspect MSBs to distinguish FP16, FP32, and FP64 in a unified register file. Default assumed: instruction opcode type dictates format at writeback.

Driver of the x0 vs x2.5 multiplier: Figure 5(c) indicates 'x0 or x2.5' downstream of WT Sigma per bank, but does not explicitly draw the control line. Default assumed: activated when the selected register's aggregate usefulness score across UT0..UT2 is greater than 0.

Pipeline squash restoration for register tracking table: whether pending entries cleared on squashes can roll back to previous architectural digests or are strictly marked invalid until re-written. Default assumed: marked invalid.
